plates.title: Lattice
plates.body: A repeating cell carries force outward rather than down, so the whole surface shares the work. Depth reads as pattern before it reads as strength.

plates.title: Cantilever
plates.body: Mass held out past its support. The drama is entirely in what you cannot see: the counterweight buried behind the wall.

plates.title: Truss
plates.body: Triangles refuse to deform. Everything above is a consequence of that one fact.

collections.label: Light
collections.blurb: What the surface does with it.

plates.title: Caustic
plates.body: Curved water focuses light into moving lines on the floor beneath. The pattern is a lens, not a texture.

plates.title: Penumbra
plates.body: The soft edge where a shadow is only partly blocked. Its width tells you how large the source was.

plates.title: Refraction
plates.body: A change of speed at a boundary bends the path. Every lens is an argument about where the image should land.

plates.title: Cadence
plates.body: Repetition with a stress pattern. The interval matters more than the event.

plates.title: Drift
plates.body: Slow displacement with no obvious force behind it. Legible only by comparison with where things were.

plates.title: Impulse
plates.body: All of the force delivered in almost none of the time. The shape of the response outlives the cause.

plates.title: Patina
plates.body: Oxidation as a finish rather than a failure. The colour is a record of exposure.

plates.title: Grain
plates.body: Direction inherited from growth. Cut across it and the material behaves like a different substance.

plates.title: Sinter
plates.body: Particles fused below their melting point. Strength arrives without ever becoming liquid.

plates.title: Tessellation
plates.body: Shapes that tile without gap or overlap. There are only seventeen ways to repeat symmetrically on a plane.

plates.title: Moire
plates.body: Two regular grids at a slight angle produce a third pattern belonging to neither.

plates.title: Voronoi
plates.body: Every point belongs to its nearest seed. Cell walls are simply the places that cannot decide.

collections.label: Scale
collections.blurb: The same thing at three sizes.

plates.title: Macro
plates.body: Close enough that surface becomes structure and the object loses its outline.

plates.title: Human
plates.body: Sized against reach, stride, and eye height. The only scale that feels like nothing at all.

plates.title: Territory
plates.body: Large enough that it can only be inferred, never seen. Maps are the interface.
